papers.title: An AI-Enabled Predictive Procurement Model for Forecasting and Inventory Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper presents an AI-enabled predictive procurement model that integrates probabilistic demand forecasting, supplier lead-time prediction, and multi-echelon inventory optimization to secure target service levels while lowering working capital. The framework couples hierarchical time-series forecasting with gradient-boosted trees and lightweight sequence models, capturing seasonality, promotions, and regime shifts. It augments predictions with causal drivers including macroeconomic indicators, input price indices, marketing calendars, and policy shocks, producing calibrated distributions rather than point estimates. Operationally, the system ingests ERP and MRP transactions, purchase orders, invoices, catalog attributes, and supplier performance histories. Data quality pipelines execute de-duplication, unit harmonization, outlier handling, and late-arrival correction, while item-location-supplier embeddings transfer information across sparse series. Lead-time models use gradient boosting with monotonic constraints on distance and order size, and a compact LSTM captures intra-week receipt patterns. Forecast reconciliation ensures coherence from SKU to category to enterprise, and conformal prediction yields reliable uncertainty bounds. Optimization formulates a newsvendor-style objective that balances service penalties, holding, and ordering costs under budget and capacity constraints. A stochastic program solved on a rolling horizon outputs order quantities, reorder points, supplier splits, and dynamic safety-stock buffers aligned to service targets. A policy engine encodes guardrails shelflife limits, ABC/XYZ policies, MOQ/pack constraints, and ESG exclusions and writes approved plans back to ERP via governed APIs and event streams with full traceability. In simulation and a limited field pilot, the approach reduced backorders and emergency expedites, lowered average on-hand inventory, and improved forecast bias and MAPE relative to baseline heuristics, with the largest gains on intermittent-demand SKUs. Ablation studies show probabilistic lead-time modeling and cross-series transfer contribute most to service-level stability. Governance artifacts, change-management practices, and value tracking methods are provided to support scale-out across plants and regions. The contribution is a production-ready, interpretable design that turns uncertainty-aware predictions into auditable, financially grounded procurement decisions embedded in day-to-day workflows. We also outline model risk management, privacy safeguards, and human-in-the-loop review to maintain accountability, fairness, and resilience under data shifts and supplier disruptions globally

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation(TMS) for Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by impairments in social communication, repetitive behaviors, sensory processing abnormalities, and variable cognitive deficits. Despite significant advances in behavioral therapies and pharmacological interventions, effective treatments capable of directly modulating dysfunctional neural networks remain limited. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) has emerged as a promising non-invasive neuromodulation technique that can alter cortical excitability, enhance neuroplasticity, and potentially improve cognitive and behavioral outcomes. Simultaneously, recent developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Digital Twin technologies have created new opportunities to personalize TMS protocols using multimodal patient data, including structural and functional neuroimaging, electroencephalography (EEG), behavioral assessments, genetic information, and longitudinal clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Impact of the Process Atmosphere During Hot Isostatic Pressing on the Near‐Surface Composition of an Additively Manufactured Austenitic High‐Interstitial Steel
papers.abstract: High interstitial steels (HIS) combine high corrosion resistance, strength, and ductility while being Ni‐free, making them cost‐efficient starting material for additive manufacturing (AM), particularly laser powder bed fusion (PBF‐LB/M), of components for demanding applications. The Fe–Mn–Cr–(C) system forms the basis of HIS and provides high N solubility, primary austenitic solidification, and a stable austenitic matrix. However, Mn and N evaporate at elevated melt pool temperatures, promoting pore formation during PBF‐LB/M. To obtain fully dense material hot isostatic pressing (HIP) is routinely applied. However, little is known about the temperature‐ and pressure‐dependent interactions between the HIP atmosphere and the AM part, especially concerning N and Mn. In this study, the effect of the Ar and N 2 HIP atmospheres on the near‐surface composition and microstructure of PBF‐LB/M‐processed HIS was investigated. By means of glow discharge optical emission spectrometry, electron microscopy, X‐ray diffraction, and CALPHAD, a distinct influence of the process gas on local chemical and phase composition was revealed. The N 2 atmosphere led to an approximately tenfold N enrichment at the surface and to Cr nitride precipitation. Ar atmosphere leads to near‐surface Mn and N depletion. Optimized HIP parameters for the postprocessing of HIS are proposed.

papers.abstract: The article considers the problem of effective formation of labeled training samples in classification and computer vision tasks under conditions of limited amount of annotated data. The relevance of the study is due to the increasing complexity of modern machine learning models, which require significant amounts of qualitatively labeled data to achieve high accuracy. At the same time, the process of expert labeling of information is laborious, financially costly and often limits the possibilities of scaling intelligent systems in practical applications.The aim of the work is to develop an approach to optimizing the process of forming labeled data based on the integration of Active Learning and semi-supervised learning methods. The study analyzes modern scientific approaches to the active selection of informative examples and the use of unlabeled data in the process of training machine learning models. Based on this, a conceptual model of an integrated learning system is proposed, which combines mechanisms of active data selection, pseudo-label generation and iterative updating of model parameters.The paper develops an extended mathematical model of an integrated approach based on Bayesian estimation of forecast uncertainty and the use of information value criteria for selecting examples from an unlabeled data pool. This approach allows you to direct the annotation process to the most informative objects and effectively use large arrays of unlabeled data in the semi-supervised learning mode.The results of the experimental study demonstrate that the proposed integrated model allows you to achieve high classification accuracy even under conditions of a significant reduction in the proportion of labeled data. The combination of Active Learning and semi-supervised learning ensures increased efficiency in the use of training samples and reduced costs for the annotation process. The results obtained confirm the prospects for applying the proposed approach in the development of intelligent image analysis systems, video analytics, medical diagnostics and other applied computer vision systems

papers.title: Rhizosphere Microbiome Engineering for Climate-Smart Agriculture: From Synthetic Consortia to Precision Decision Support
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microbiome engineering is a promising approach that can enhance crop resilience and input use efficiency by redirecting plant–microbe–soil interactions toward predictable functions. Here, we review the mechanistic bases underlying rhizosphere assembly and stability, including root exudate-mediated selection, priority effects, keystone taxa, and metabolite-driven signaling, and connect these principles to proposed design rules for microbial inoculants. We present a generalizable Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) framework for engineering synthetic microbial consortia, covering trait-to-module mapping (nutrient acquisition, phytohormone modulation, ACC deaminase activity, stress-protective metabolites, and biocontrol), compatibility screening, minimal yet robust community architectures, and iterative optimization driven by multi-omics and high-throughput phenotyping. Translation to field settings is framed as an engineering challenge defined by formulation and administration limitations, including carrier type, seed coating and encapsulation methods, shelf life, strain invasiveness, and permanence of colonization amid environmental diversity. We also summarize how integrative measurement pipelines (amplicon and shotgun sequencing, transcriptomics, metabolomics, and network or causal analyses) can advance microbiome studies from correlation to actionability. We describe how precision agriculture (sensors, remote sensing, and variable-rate inputs) and AI/ML (split-sample comparisons, transfer learning, and active learning) approaches can accelerate strain discovery, mixture optimization, and adaptive experimentation, driven by the need for stringent controls, metadata-rich reporting, and cross-site comparability. Use cases focus on stress conditions (drought, salinity, thermal extremes, and biotic stress) to demonstrate how microbial functions translate to agronomic outcomes and to highlight critical bottlenecks for reproducible, scalable microbiome products.

papers.title: Biomaterials and scaffolds that promote regenerative rather than fibrotic healing
papers.abstract: Wound healing after dermal wounding is a major clinical problem and for adult skin, healing reverts to fibrotic repair, which involves an excess of collagen deposition and an activation of myofibroblasts. Embryonic skin, on the other hand, quickly regenerates without scarring, with tightly regulated immune responses and balanced cytokine signaling. The biomaterial scaffolds have been developed to become active therapeutic platforms that can alter the course of the wound from fibrosis to regeneration by mimicking essential microenvironmental signals. Scaffold design principles (architecture, porosity, stiffness, and surface topography) are discussed and natural and synthetic biomaterials are reviewed for their ability to induce regeneration associated phenotypes. We highlight immune-modulatory strategies which switch macrophages to pro-resolving phenotypes and inhibit fibrotic cascade. In addition to state of the art fabrication technologies like 3D bioprinting and electrospinning, advanced biofunctionalization strategies like sustained delivery of anti-fibrotic growth factors, miRNA therapeutics and cell-seeded constructs are also critically evaluated. Preliminary data have shown that strategically designed scaffolds can markedly decrease scar index and restore skin appendages. Lastly, we discuss translational issues and trends for personalized, phase-dependent responsive scaffolds. This analysis emphasizes that biomaterial-directed regeneration is a pedagogic therapeutic model that can revolutionize scar management in the clinical practice.

papers.title: Impacto da ansiedade matemática na aprendizagem escolar: uma revisão sistemática
papers.abstract: Mathematics anxiety (MA) is an emotional phenomenon that can significantly affect students' learning and academic performance. In this context, the present study aimed to analyze the causes, impacts, and coping strategies related to mathematics anxiety among Basic Education students. To achieve this objective, a systematic literature review was conducted based on the PRISMA guidelines, using studies retrieved from the CAPES Journal Portal. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, six studies were selected for analysis. The findings revealed that mathematics anxiety is influenced by emotional, social, and pedagogical factors, including inadequate teaching methodologies, negative classroom experiences, family influences, and unfavorable attitudes of teachers toward Mathematics. The results also indicated that MA is associated with lower academic achievement, impairments in working memory, avoidance behaviors, and reduced engagement with the subject. On the other hand, the analyzed studies suggest that active learning methodologies, playful activities, educational games, practices based on Flow Theory, cognitive tutoring programs, and supportive learning environments can help reduce anxiety levels. Furthermore, evidence from neuroscience suggests that regular physical exercise may contribute to emotional regulation and cognitive performance. It is concluded that addressing mathematics anxiety requires integrated actions involving schools, teachers, and families, as well as investments in teacher education and pedagogical practices that promote support, confidence, and student autonomy.

papers.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Optimization-Based Preprocessing Methods of Ewing Sarcoma X-ray Imaging
papers.abstract: Ewing Sarcoma (ES) is a malignant bone and soft tissue tumor belonging to the Ewing Sarcoma Family of Tumors (ESFT), affecting children and adolescents with a peak incidence at 15 years. As an ESFT tumor, its symptoms overlap with those of other related tumors; This necessitates the use of diagnostic tools-such as medical imaging- in addition to microscopic analysis and etiological investigation. X-ray emerges as a suitable solution due to its cost-effectiveness and widespread availability. However, for certain diseases, the availability of clear images and a sufficient quantity thereof poses a significant challenge. To address this challenge, this article investigates the impact of enhancement techniques on the quality of the X-ray images. A total of 4900 X-rays were used to evaluate the 3 preprocessing approaches: a baseline method combining median filtering, Wiener filtering, and CLAHE; a proposed method integrating artifact removal, enhanced bony structure, and Bayesian optimization of CLAHE parameters; and an extended approach incorporating adaptive gamma correction. The performance of each approach was evaluated using quantitative metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Edge Preservation Index (EPI). On the ES images, the proposed method reduced the average MSE from 79.88 to 55.44, while increasing PSNR from 22.43 dB to 25.90 dB and improving SSIM from 0.837 to 0.912. On the healthy dataset, the MSE decreased from 74.73 to 45.42, PSNR increased to 28.41 dB, and SSIM reached 0.911. The proposed method also achieved competitive edge preservation, confirming its ability to maintain structural integrity.

papers.title: Teachers’ Digital Competence and Student’s Engagement in Select Districts of Misamis Oriental Division
papers.abstract: Teachers’ digital competence plays a crucial role in integrating technology into classroom instruction to enhance students’ academic experiences and engagement. This study determined the extent of teachers' digital competence and students' learning engagement in select districts of Misamis Oriental Division during the School Year 2024–2025. Specifically, it aimed to find out the gap of technology-integration instruction. It employed a descriptive-correlational research design, data were gathered using a validated researcher-made questionnaire administered to 213 secondary school teachers selected through total population sampling and 426 secondary school students chosen via simple random sampling, analyzed through descriptive and inferential statistics such as the mean and standard deviation to describe the variables in the study. Furthermore, Pearson-product moment correlation coefficient (r) was also employed to determine the significant relationship among the variables. Findings revealed that teachers demonstrated a high level of digital competence, particularly in Delivery and Students’ Support, while School Development showed the lowest level while students demonstrated a moderate level of engagement, with Collaboration and Support obtaining the highest level and Learning Environment the lowest. Further, there was no significant relationship between teachers' digital competence and student engagement. It is concluded that high teacher digital literacy does not automatically translate into high student engagement as tool usage alone is insufficient towards active learning. It is recommended that teachers should utilize technology to promote collaborative learning through digital platforms, interactive communication using tools and the personalized learning experiences in facilitating learning environment. They should explore topics that interest students beyond classroom lessons.

papers.title: Magnetically Responsive TPMS-Based Smart Scaffold for Bone Tissue Engineering: Numerical Investigation Using COMSOL Multiphysics
papers.abstract: Magnetically responsive scaffolds have emerged as promising platforms in tissue engineering due to their ability to provide remote, non-invasive stimulation for regulating cellular behavior and enhancing tissue regeneration. In this study, a novel triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS)-based smart scaffold reinforced with superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) was designed and numerically investigated using COMSOL Multiphysics®. The scaffold architecture was optimized to combine high porosity, interconnected pore networks, and magnetic responsiveness for bone tissue engineering applications. A three-dimensional finite element model was developed to analyze magnetic flux density distribution, field intensity, and magnetic field propagation under an external static magnetic field. Simulations were performed using Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinate systems to comprehensively evaluate magnetic behavior within and around the scaffold structure. The results demonstrated homogeneous magnetic field penetration throughout the porous architecture, with localized magnetic flux enhancement observed at pore-wall intersections and regions of high curvature. The maximum magnetic flux density reached approximately 2.08 mT, which lies within the biologically effective range reported for osteogenic stimulation. The proposed scaffold generated controllable magnetic microenvironments capable of enhancing mechanotransduction pathways, promoting cell proliferation, and supporting bone regeneration. The findings suggest that TPMS-based magnetic scaffolds represent a promising strategy for next-generation smart biomaterials and magnetically controlled regenerative therapies.
